cells.tense: Right now you can hold your group's feeling and its shape without forcing either one.
cells.ask: Choose a practice your people keep out of habit and give it a solid piece that no longer leans on your hand. A written note, a fixed date, a named person — something that keeps after you stop standing over it.
cells.core:
You can sit in a group where something matters and hold its feeling without making anybody perform it. The tradition stays alive because you keep the space where it lives, and no one has to be told to be moved by it. What you carry is real, and it stays light because your grip is loose.

Give one piece of it a shape that holds after you step away. Pick a practice your people keep — a meal, a gathering, a way of marking a season — and make one part of it solid enough to survive a week without your attention. Set it down where it gets picked up, or hand it to someone. You will still be part of it. More of it will be, too.
cells.sheetLine: You keep your group's feeling level and its story alive.
cells.verb: tending the shared story so the group stays level and no one is left holding it alone
cells.place: at the table where a group keeps what it has always done

cells.tense: Soon you will be holding your group's shared meaning so tight that nothing in it can shift.
cells.act: release what is done and keep what serves
cells.ask: Find a practice your group keeps only because it was once right, and finish it this week without a replacement. Tell those who count on it, plainly, that it is over. Name what still feeds you, so no one believes the whole thing is closing.
cells.core:
Where a group keeps its shared meaning, your care has become a grip. You are bracing for a room that will need you before it needs anything else, holding the feeling of those in it so it cannot shift under its own weight. What was tending has hardened into holding, and the people inside can feel the walls.

Some of what you carry is finished. Take a practice your people keep only because it was once right, and finish it — no replacement, no ceremony. Say plainly that it is over, and say what still feeds you, so the room knows not everything is shutting. Endings that are honored make room for what comes next. Your group can hold its own weight for a week.

cells.tense: Your group's shared story is one you now watch from outside it.
cells.act: say the hard thing gently, once
cells.ask: Set down a piece of your group's shared story that you carry alone, in plain words, no audience, and read it back. Then decide, on your own, if anyone needs to hear it. They may not.
cells.core:
Where a group keeps its shared meaning, you have stepped back from the part you used to take. The story your people tell themselves is still going, and you are not adding to it the way you once did — watching is what you do now, without saying so. The feeling is still yours. It just has not been brought into the open.

Here is one small way back. Take a piece of the shared story you carry alone — something you know about how your people came to do what they do — and put it into plain words for yourself, no audience. Read it back. Then decide, quietly, whether anyone else needs to hear it; they may not, and that is allowed. Putting a true thing clearly, once, is already what you do well.

cells.tense: You are keeping your group's shared meaning level while telling yourself you are only passing through.
cells.act: cut to the logic and act on it
cells.ask: Recall a time this month when a group you are part of stayed level because of something you did and did not name. Put what you actually did in one plain sentence and keep it where you will see it. That is all.
cells.core:
Your group's shared meaning holds around you — a phrase placed, a weight shifted — and your account of yourself is that you are not really part of it. The work is happening. The story you tell is that you just happen to be nearby, and the people who feel the room hold have not bought that story once.

There is a cleaner way to see it. Think of one time this month when the group stayed level because of something you did — not something you felt, something you did — and put it in one plain sentence. Keep the page where you will see it; no one else needs to read it. Looking straight at a fact is what makes the work visible to the one doing it. Nothing changes in the group. Something changes in the account.
cells.sheetLine: The group stays level because of you, and you say you are just passing through.
cells.verb: tending the shared story so the group stays level and no one is left holding it alone
cells.place: at the table where a group keeps what it has always done

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is in the Too Little cell — I say the person has stopped bringing feeling into the shared room, when the record only shows under-expression, not that they were once present and withdrew. A reader could reasonably say they were never in that room to begin with, or that the absence is chosen, not a wound. The ask (write down one piece of the shared story you've been keeping private, in its plainest form, then decide what to do with the page) survives being wrong: it teaches the person something about their own relation to the room's story regardless of whether the absence is pain or preference. The sentence that serves me more than them is any line that turns the silence into a verdict; I've cut those and left the absence as a fact they can recognize or refuse.
